name: Gilt market
summary: 10-year gilt yield 5.18% on 27 Nov, 17bp lower on the month but 73bp higher on the year
state: The 10-year gilt yield was 5.18% on 27 Nov, 2bp up on the day, 17bp lower on the month and 73bp higher than a year earlier (Trading Economics). It peaked above 5.35% on 16 Nov as markets priced a December Bank of England rise. The monthly move is inside the 40bp line and no weak auction or BoE intervention was found; Watch is kept under hysteresis while yields stay near multi-year highs.
for_you: Mortgage and loan rates linked to gilt yields remain high. Households refinancing fixed-rate mortgages face higher costs than a year ago.
rubric_hit: Yields near multi-year highs; 10y 1m move -17bp < 40bp; Watch kept under hysteresis

sources.title: Bank of England — Financial Stability Report, November 2026

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
